as_told.title: Bondi's question on positivity conditions at Chapel Hill

plain: At a 1957 physics conference in Chapel Hill, North Carolina, where Michels says quantum gravity was set up as a field, the Austrian mathematician Hermann Bondi gave a talk on negative mass in general relativity. Michels passes this on from the researcher Eric Weinstein, who poses Bondi's point as a question about whether mass must always be positive. Michels says he has the conference report, The Role of Gravitation in Physics, which has a chapter on Bondi's talk; for Michels this means serious physicists were weighing ideas that bear on pushing against gravity.
